acctCDNBucketsHelp: Optional. Bucket names, separated by commas, that get CDN links. Leave empty to use the CDN URL for every bucket of this account.
acctCDNURLHelp: Optional. The address your CDN serves objects from. A base URL such as https://cdn.example.com gives links like base/bucket/key. For a custom link, write a template with '{bucket}' and '{key}'; a template that uses '{bucket}' needs '{key}' as well.
acctChecksumModeHelp: Controls the integrity checksums added to uploads and checked on downloads. Auto uses the SDK default on AWS and sends only the required checksums to S3-compatible services. Choose When required if a service rejects uploads; choose When supported to always send them.
acctCredentialsHelp: Access keys: an access key ID and secret key stored on this computer. AWS profile: a named profile from your AWS shared config and credentials files. Default chain: the standard AWS SDK lookup of environment variables, shared files, then instance or container roles. Anonymous: unsigned requests, for public buckets only.
acctEndpointHelp: The full address of the service, starting with http:// or https://, without credentials or a query string.
acctErrCDNTemplate: CDN URL template with '{bucket}' must also contain '{key}'
acctErrCDNURL: CDN URL must be an http(s) URL without credentials, query or fragment
acctErrEndpointScheme: Use an http:// or https:// URL
acctErrRole: A role ARN starts with arn:
acctErrSession: Enter the secret access key as well to change the token
acctExternalIDHelp: Optional. The external ID the role's trust policy requires when it is assumed. Only used together with a role ARN.
acctKeepSecret: Leave empty to keep the current secret
acctPathStyleHelp: Addresses objects as endpoint/bucket/object. MinIO and most self-hosted gateways need this on; keep it off for AWS.
acctProfileHelp: The name of a profile in your AWS shared config and credentials files, for example default.
acctProviderHelp: AWS connects to Amazon S3. S3-compatible connects to another service at an endpoint you enter, such as MinIO or a self-hosted gateway.
acctRegionHelp: The region requests are signed for, such as us-east-1. Leave the default unless your service asks for a specific region.
acctRemoveMessage: This only removes the saved connection and its stored credentials from this computer. Your buckets and objects in the cloud are not affected.
acctRoleARNHelp: Optional. An IAM role to assume with the credentials above; all requests then use that role. It must start with arn: and cannot be combined with anonymous access.
acctSecretMissing: The secret access key of this account is missing. Enter it again to reconnect.
acctSessionNameHelp: Optional. The name of the assumed-role session, shown in AWS logs such as CloudTrail. Leave empty for an automatic name. Only used together with a role ARN.
acctSessionTokenHelp: Only needed for temporary credentials, for example from AWS STS. It is stored with the secret key, so enter the secret key again when you change it.
acctSetupVaultTip: Store credentials in an encrypted vault instead
acctSkipTLSHelp: Turns off certificate checks for this connection, so a fake server could read your data and credentials. Use it only for test servers you trust, such as a local MinIO with a self-signed certificate.
actionsDownloadErrors: Download finished with errors: {done} downloaded, {failed} failed
actionsFolderExists: A folder with this name exists
actionsUploadErrors: Upload finished with errors: {done} uploaded, {failed} failed
aliasTheme: appearance follow os automatic bright night mode
bucketDialogsAllVersions: Also delete all versions and delete markers
bucketDialogsAllVersionsHelp: Without this, a versioned bucket keeps its older versions and only gains delete markers, so it still holds data.
bucketDialogsNameChars: Use lowercase letters, digits, periods and hyphens
bucketDialogsNameEdges: Start and end with a lowercase letter or digit
bucketDialogsNameHint: 3 to 63 characters: a-z, 0-9, periods and hyphens. The name cannot be changed later.
bucketDialogsNameIpLike: The name must not look like an IP address
bucketDialogsNamePeriods: No two periods in a row
bucketDialogsNameSuffix: The name must not end with -s3alias or --ol-s3
bucketDialogsNameXn: The name must not start with xn--
bucketDialogsObjectLockHelp: Creates the bucket with Object Lock on, which also turns versioning on. It can only be chosen here, when the bucket is created.
bucketDialogsRegionHelp: The region where the bucket is created. It cannot be changed afterwards.
bucketDialogsTypeName: Type the bucket name to confirm
bucketSettingsAccelerateHelp: Lets clients use the bucket's accelerated endpoint, which routes long-distance transfers through AWS edge locations, for an additional fee. Pail only switches the setting; its own transfers keep using the normal endpoint. Providers without this feature report it as unsupported.
bucketSettingsCorsHelp: JSON rules (CORSRules) that tell browsers which web origins may call this bucket and with which methods.
bucketSettingsDefaultEncryptionHelp: SSE-S3 (AES-256) lets S3 manage the keys; AWS KMS encrypts with a KMS key. Applies to new uploads only.
bucketSettingsEncryptionHelp: The default server-side encryption for objects uploaded without their own setting. Existing objects are not changed; use Change encryption for those. Choosing None removes the default.
bucketSettingsKmsKeyIdHelp: A key ID, key ARN or alias. Leave it empty to use the AWS managed key.
bucketSettingsLifecycleHelp: JSON rules (Rules) that expire objects or move them to another storage class after a set time.
bucketSettingsLoggingHelp: Delivers the access logs of this bucket to a target bucket and prefix (LoggingEnabled). The target bucket must allow log delivery.
bucketSettingsNeverVersioned: Versioning has never been enabled for this bucket.
bucketSettingsNotObject: The configuration must be a JSON object
bucketSettingsObjectLockHelp: Sets the default retention (mode and period) that new object versions receive. It cannot be removed here.
bucketSettingsOwnershipHelp: Decides who owns objects uploaded by other accounts and whether ACLs still apply. Bucket owner enforced turns ACLs off.
bucketSettingsPabAclsHelp: Rejects requests that try to set a public ACL on the bucket or its objects.
bucketSettingsPabIgnoreAclsHelp: Ignores all public ACLs on the bucket and its objects, including ones that already exist.
bucketSettingsPabPolicyHelp: Rejects bucket policies that grant public access.
bucketSettingsPabRestrictHelp: Limits access to a bucket that has a public policy to AWS services and authorized users of this account.
bucketSettingsPolicyHelp: A JSON bucket policy that allows or denies access to this bucket. The text is sent as written and the service validates it.
bucketSettingsPublicAccessHelp: Switches that block public ACLs and public bucket policies. Leave them on unless the bucket must serve public content.
bucketSettingsRemoveMessage: The bucket goes back to the provider's default for this setting.
bucketSettingsReplicationHelp: Copies new objects to another bucket (Destination) with a role that S3 can assume (Role). Versioning must be on in both buckets.
bucketSettingsRequesterHelp: When on, whoever downloads from this bucket pays the request and transfer costs instead of the bucket owner.
bucketSettingsTagsHelp: Tags (TagSet) on the bucket itself, for example for cost allocation. Tags of objects are edited in the Inspector.
bucketSettingsVersioningHelp: Keeps older versions when an object is overwritten or deleted. Suspending stops new versions from being kept; the versions already stored remain.
bucketSettingsWebsiteHelp: Serves the bucket as a static website with an index document and an error document, or redirects all requests.
cdnUrlsCopied: {n, plural, one {# CDN URL copied} other {# CDN URLs copied}}
clipboardCopiedFailed: Copied {items}, {failed, plural, one {# failed} other {# failed}}
clipboardCopiedSkipped: Copied {items}, {skipped, plural, one {# skipped} other {# skipped}}
clipboardCrossAccount: Copying between accounts is not supported yet
clipboardMovedFailed: Moved {items}, {failed, plural, one {# failed} other {# failed}}
clipboardMovedSkipped: Moved {items}, {skipped, plural, one {# skipped} other {# skipped}}
cloudfrontAwsOnly: CloudFront is available for AWS accounts
cloudfrontInvalidationsHelp: An invalidation asks CloudFront to drop its cached copies of the listed paths. It runs in the background and shows InProgress until it is done; the list refreshes every 10 seconds while one is in progress.
cloudfrontPathsHelp: One path per line, starting with /. A * is only allowed as the last character and matches everything below that point (/images/*, or /* for everything). One request takes up to 3,000 paths.
cloudfrontPathsPh: One path per line, e.g. /index.html or /images/*
editAclCannedHelp: A canned ACL is a ready-made set of grants for this object. Private keeps it to the owner; the public options let anyone read it, or read and write it.
editAclChangeWhat: change the permissions of this object
editAclDisabled: ACLs are disabled for this bucket
editAclPublicRWMsg: The object becomes publicly readable and writable by anyone.
editAclPublicReadMsg: The object becomes publicly readable by anyone with its address.
editAclReadWhat: read the permissions of this object
editPropsHeadersHelp: The standard HTTP headers stored with the object and sent back when it is downloaded. Clear a value to remove that header.
editPropsHeadersMultiHelp: A change is applied to every selected object, and to everything inside selected folders. Fields where the objects differ keep each object's own value until you edit them.
editPropsHelpCacheControl: Tells browsers and CDNs how long they may cache the object, for example max-age=3600.
editPropsHelpContentDisposition: Decides whether browsers show the object (inline) or save it as a file (attachment; filename=name.ext).
editPropsHelpContentEncoding: Set gzip or br only if the stored bytes really are compressed that way; clients then decompress the object when they download it.
editPropsHelpContentLanguage: The language of the content, such as en or zh-CN.
editPropsHelpContentType: The media type, such as text/html or image/png. Browsers use it to decide how to open the object.
editPropsHelpExpires: The date after which caches treat the object as stale, written as an HTTP date such as Mon, 02 Jan 2006 15:04:05 GMT.
editPropsMetadataHelp: Custom key-value pairs stored with the object and sent back as x-amz-meta-* headers. Keys are saved in lower case, everything must be plain ASCII, and the total is limited to 2 KiB.
editPropsNotApplied: the change could not be applied
editPropsUpdateMessage: Every selected object is rewritten in place.
editTagsHelp: Key-value labels on the object (up to 10) that lifecycle rules, cost reports and access policies can match. Keys starting with aws: are reserved.
editTagsReserved: Keys starting with aws: are reserved
inspectorStillLoading: Still loading — totals cover what is listed so far
bucketCopyMoveWarning: Each object is deleted from {bucket} once it is copied. This cannot be undone.
bucketCopyNoOther: There is no other bucket in this account
bucketCopyPrefixPlaceholder: Bucket root, or a folder such as backup/
bucketCopyTargetPrefixHelp: Objects are copied under this prefix and keep their own key path. Leave it empty to copy to the bucket root.
flatListTip: List every object below this folder, sub-folders included, as one flat list. Folders are not shown.
flatListUnavailable: Not available while deleted items are shown
mimeContentTypeHelp: The Content-Type sent when a file with this extension is uploaded. Extensions not listed here use the operating system table, then application/octet-stream.
mimeEnterType: Enter a content type such as text/plain
mimeExtensionHelp: The leading dot is optional and the case does not matter (svg and .SVG both mean .svg). Each extension can be listed once.
mimeTestHelp: Shows the Content-Type an upload of this file name would get from the table above, including unsaved edits. An upload rule that sets Content-Type still takes precedence.
multipartAbortMessage: {n, plural, one {# unfinished upload and the parts already sent will be discarded. This cannot be undone.} other {# unfinished uploads and the parts already sent will be discarded. This cannot be undone.}}
multipartHelp: An unfinished multipart upload keeps the parts already sent in the bucket and is billed as storage until it is completed or aborted. This list shows the unfinished uploads under the prefix; Abort deletes the parts of the selected ones.
objectsEmptySub: Upload files or create a folder
objectsNoDeletedSub: Nothing here has a delete marker
pathbarNoVersionsTip: This bucket has no versions, so nothing can be restored
pathbarShowDeletedTip: Show deleted items: objects whose latest version is a delete marker, so you can restore them. Only for buckets that have versioning.
previewFirstRows: {n, plural, one {Showing the first # row} other {Showing the first # rows}}
renameFileExists: A file with this name exists
renameFolderExists: A folder with this name exists
rewriteClassCanceled: Changing the storage class was canceled
rewriteClassDone: Storage class set to {value} on {n, plural, one {# object} other {# objects}}
rewriteClassFailed: Could not change the storage class: {detail}
rewriteClassHelp: Colder classes cost less to store but more to read, and archived objects must be restored before they can be read. Each object is copied onto itself to change its class, so archived objects that are not restored and SSE-C objects fail individually.
rewriteClassInvalid: Use capital letters, digits and underscores
rewriteClassPartial: Changed the storage class of {ok, plural, one {# object} other {# objects}}, {failed, plural, one {# failed} other {# failed}}
rewriteEncDone: Encryption set to {value} on {n, plural, one {# object} other {# objects}}
rewriteEncHelp: SSE-S3 (AES256): S3 manages the keys. SSE-KMS: an AWS KMS key encrypts the object. SSE-C: the key is supplied by the user, needs an https endpoint, and the object can only be read with that key. None drops the explicit setting; a bucket default may still apply.
rewriteEncPartial: Changed the encryption of {ok, plural, one {# object} other {# objects}}, {failed, plural, one {# failed} other {# failed}}
rewriteKmsKeyHelp: A key ID, key ARN or alias. Leave it empty to use the AWS managed key.
rewriteKmsPlaceholder: Key ID or ARN (blank: the AWS managed key)
rewriteNote: Rewrites each object; versioned buckets keep the previous version.
rewriteNothing: Nothing to change: {n, plural, one {# object} other {# objects}} already set
rewriteSsecKeyHelp: A saved secret reference that holds a base64-encoded 32-byte key. The key is sent with every request, so the endpoint must use https.
rulesBucketMaskHelp: Matches the bucket name, case-sensitive. * stands for any characters and ? for exactly one; leave empty to match every bucket.
rulesCompressionHelp: GZIP keeps the object key and sets Content-Encoding: gzip. ZIP and AES-256 ZIP upload one .zip object (the key gets .zip added). Do not combine either with a Content-Encoding header.
rulesEncryptionHelp: AES256 uses S3-managed keys, aws:kms uses an AWS KMS key, and SSE-C encrypts with a 32-byte key kept as a secret (it needs an https endpoint). None asks for no encryption.
rulesHeadersHelp: Standard headers stored on the object: Cache-Control, Content-Disposition, Content-Encoding, Content-Language, Content-Type and Expires. A Content-Type set here overrides the MIME types table (except for ZIP output).
rulesKeyMaskHelp: Matches the whole object key, case-sensitive. * matches any characters including /, so images/*.png also matches images/a/b.png; ? matches one character. Leave empty to match every key.
rulesKeyRefHelp: Name of a saved secret that holds the 32-byte key as base64 text. Add it under Manage secrets…; the key itself is never stored in the rule.
rulesKmsKeyIdHelp: ID or ARN of the KMS key to encrypt with. Optional: without it the server uses its default KMS key.
rulesLevelHelp: 0 stores the file without compressing it, 9 compresses the most and is slowest. Default balances the two; Huffman only is fast but compresses little.
rulesMetadataHelp: Custom key-value pairs saved as user metadata on the object (S3 stores the keys in lower case). Use these for anything that is not a standard header.
rulesOrderHelp: Rules are checked from top to bottom. For each kind of setting (headers and metadata, storage class, encryption, compression) the first matching rule that sets it wins, so put specific rules above general ones.
rulesPasswordHelp: Name of a saved secret used as the ZIP password. Keep that password safe: it is needed to open the file, and the rule stores only its name.
rulesProblemExpires: rule {n} ({name}): Expires must be an HTTP date such as Wed, 21 Oct 2026 07:28:00 GMT
rulesProblemPassword: Choose a password reference for AES-256 ZIP
rulesStorageClassHelp: Storage class given to matching uploads. Default sends none, so the server default applies (normally Standard).
rulesTestHelp: Shows the settings these rules, including unsaved edits, would apply to an upload to this bucket and key.
secretsDeleteMessage: Rules that use this reference fail until it exists again.
settingsConflictHelp: Applies to uploads, downloads and, as the default, copying or moving between buckets. Keep both: the new item gets a numbered name such as report (1).pdf and nothing is replaced. Skip existing: the existing item is left alone and the new one is skipped. Overwrite: the existing item is always replaced. Overwrite if newer: replaced only when the new item was modified more recently. Overwrite if size differs: replaced only when the sizes differ.
settingsDirHelp: Where downloads are saved without asking. Leave it empty to choose a folder every time. Use a full path.
settingsDownloadsNHelp: How many download tasks run at the same time; the rest wait in the queue. Lowering it never interrupts a running task. Allowed: 1 to 64.
settingsErrNumber: Enter a whole number from {lo} to {hi}{unit}
settingsLanguageHelp: Follow system uses your operating system's language and falls back to English. The choice is remembered.
settingsLogHelp: Writes errors and task results to a log file for troubleshooting (3 files of up to 5 MiB each). File and bucket names can appear in it. Secret keys, session tokens, passwords, signatures and URL query strings are replaced with [REDACTED]. Off by default.
settingsLogOpenFail: Could not open the log folder: {detail}
settingsOtherHelp: How many other tasks, such as copying, moving or deleting objects, run at the same time. Allowed: 1 to 64.
settingsPartHelp: The size of each part when a file is uploaded or downloaded in parts. Allowed: 5 to 5120 MiB, because S3 does not accept smaller parts. Larger parts mean fewer requests per file.
settingsThemeHelp: Choose Light or Dark, or let System follow your operating system. The change applies at once.
settingsUploadsHelp: How many upload tasks run at the same time; the rest wait in the queue. Lowering it never interrupts a running task. Allowed: 1 to 64.
settingsWorkersHelp: How many objects a single bulk task, such as a copy, move, delete or rewrite, handles in parallel. Allowed: 1 to 64.
shellWelcomeSub: Browse buckets and move files with AWS or any S3-compatible service
signedCdnCopiedMany: {n, plural, one {# CDN URL copied} other {# CDN URLs copied}}
signedCopiedMany: {n, plural, one {# signed URL copied} other {# signed URLs copied}}
signedCopyCdnTip: Copy the address the object has on the CDN
signedCopyPublicTip: Copy the address the object has when it is public
signedExpiryHelp: How long the link keeps working, up to 7 days (the S3 limit). Anyone with the link can use it until then, and links signed with temporary credentials stop when those expire.
signedMethodHelp: GET lets anyone with the link download the object. PUT lets them upload a file to this key, replacing what is there; a PUT link cannot point to a version.
signedVersionHelp: Signs one specific version of the object; leave it empty for the latest version. Only available for a GET link to a single object.
stateBucketsSecretMissing: The secret access key is missing. Enter it to reconnect.
statusbarItemsOf: {n, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} of {total}
syncChooseFirst: Choose a local folder and a bucket first
syncCompareHelp: Size and time treats a file as changed when its size differs or the modification times disagree (a download only replaces a local file with a newer object). Size compares sizes only. Checksum compares a SHA-256 saved on the object by earlier syncs; objects without one count as changed.
syncDeleteNote: Only the job is removed. Neither side is touched.
syncDeleteWill: {n, plural, one {# file will be deleted at the destination} other {# files will be deleted at the destination}}
syncDirectionHelp: Upload copies files from the local folder to the bucket prefix; Download copies objects from the bucket prefix to the local folder. A sync only ever goes one way.
syncExcludesHelp: One pattern per line, matched against the whole path relative to the sync folder, written with /. * matches any characters including /, ? one character, and a pattern ending in / excludes that folder and everything in it. Excluded files are skipped on both sides and never deleted.
syncMirrorWarning: Deletes extra files at the destination
syncModeHelp: New only copies files the destination does not have yet. New and changed also replaces files that differ (see Compare). Mirror does the same and also deletes what is missing from the source: objects in the bucket, or local files (moved to the {trash}) when downloading.
syncPreviewHelp: Reads both sides and lists what a sync would do; nothing is changed. Run sync then performs exactly these actions, without overwriting anything that changed since. Editing the job clears the preview.
syncReasonIrregular: not a regular file (device, socket or pipe)
syncReasonLongKey: object key is longer than 1024 bytes
syncReasonNoETag: the remote object has no ETag to guard the overwrite
syncReasonReparse: reparse point or irregular file (not followed)
syncTrashNote: Local files are moved to the {trash}.
toolsRulesLine: Headers, storage class, compression and encryption per path
toolsSettingsLine: Theme, concurrency, part size and downloads
toolsSyncLine: Keep a local folder and a bucket in step
typesAccessDenied: Access denied. Check the credentials and what they are allowed to do
typesLocked: The encrypted vault is locked. Enter the master password to unlock it
typesNetwork: Can't reach the server. Check the connection and the endpoint
typesNotFound: Not found. It may have been deleted or renamed
typesUnsupported: This provider does not support that
vaultAutoLockHelp: Locks the vault after this many minutes without using the stored credentials; the master password is then needed again. Never keeps it unlocked until you lock it.
vaultCreateNote: Your credentials will be encrypted with this password.
vaultExistingNote: A vault from an earlier setup was found. Enter its master password to use it.
vaultForgotten: A forgotten master password cannot be recovered.
vaultNoKeychain: No system keychain is available on this computer. Use the encrypted vault to store your credentials.
vaultNowInVault: Credentials are now in the encrypted vault
vaultRefsLost: These secret references lost their values: {names}. Add them again in Upload rules.
vaultResetAccounts: Accounts that need their secret again
vaultResetDone: Vault reset. Enter the missing secrets again
vaultResetLine1: This deletes the vault and every secret stored in it.
vaultResetLine2: It cannot be undone. Your buckets and objects in the cloud are not affected.
vaultResetRefs: Secret references that lose their value
vaultSecretMissingFor: Secret missing for {names}. Edit the account to enter it again.
vaultStorageHelp: The system keychain ({keychain}) lets the operating system hold your credentials. The encrypted vault keeps them in a file protected by a master password you choose; use it when the system has no keychain. Switching moves the stored credentials; nothing in the cloud changes.
vaultToKeychainNote: Your stored credentials move from the encrypted vault to {keychain}. The vault file is deleted afterwards.
vaultUnlockNote: Enter your master password to use the stored credentials.
versionsDeletedCount: Deleted {n, plural, one {# version} other {# versions}}
versionsDeletedPartial: Deleted {ok, plural, one {# version} other {# versions}}, {failed, plural, one {# failed} other {# failed}}
versionsListDeletedWhat: list the deleted items of this bucket
versionsListWhat: list the versions of this object
versionsRestoreAllMsg: Every deleted item below this folder gets its latest version back.
versionsRestoredItems: Restored {n, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}
versionsRestoredPartial: Restored {ok, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}, {failed, plural, one {# failed} other {# failed}}
versionsSelected: {n, plural, one {# version selected} other {# versions selected}}
